The new correction polynomial below is called C_p, to avoid collision with the independently fixed old JT2 target scalar R_p. ## Construction and descent Fix p=6m+1>=7, t=1-2x, q=4x(1-x)=1-t^2. The full Fp correction A=I-I(1)H/2 is odd under x -> 1-x. Hence the odd polynomial A((1-t)/2) has the unique form t c(t^2). Define C_p(w)=c(1-w). Then A(x)=t C_p(q) in Fp[x], deg C_p <=3m-1. This definition uses the already independent Fp I/H recurrences alone. Let Lsym=(L_p(x)+L_p(1-x))/2, over the exact p-integral rationals. After x=(1-t)/2 it is even in t. It therefore uniquely descends to an exact p-integral rational polynomial M_p(w): Lsym(x)=M_p(q), deg M_p <=3m. Both constructions are coefficient identities, not fits to a marked point. They need no division by t when evaluated at its zero: oddness first guarantees polynomial divisibility by t, and the resulting quotient is even. The reflected difference proved earlier is E-R E=A, with E=(f_p(q)-L_p)/p^2 mod p. Thus (L_p-L_p(1-x))/2 = -p^2 A/2 mod p^3, f_p(q)=Lsym+p^2(x^p-1/2)A mod p^3. In Fp[x], x^p-1/2=-t^p/2. With k=(p+1)/2=3m+1 this gives f_p(q)=M_p(q)-(p^2/2)(1-q)^k C_p(q) mod p^3. The substitution map w ->4x(1-x) is injective also over Z_p/p^3: the leading coefficient of a nonzero polynomial of degree d acquires the unit multiplier (-4)^d at degree 2d. It cannot vanish or be cancelled by lower terms. Therefore the uniform descended identity is f_p(w)=M_p(w)-(p^2/2)(1-w)^k C_p(w) mod p^3. (Q3) Any coefficient lifts of C_p give the same identity. The degrees are consistent: k+deg C_p <=(3m+1)+(3m-1)=6m=p-1, the original cutoff.
